source.check: every name and label checked against the page image; returned unopposed, no poll

note: Triennial election of the county council, 1930: nominations received by T. E. Reid, secretary, 29 April 1930; after withdrawals there was no contest in the county. Returned unopposed. The Belfast News-Letter prints his label as "U.", apparently a misprint (he is "N." in the 1924 lists); no label is filed. Thomas Mallon: no party label printed in 1930. At other elections he stood as Nationalist (Keady, Keady Urban District, 15 January 1926, printed 'Nat.': Belfast News-Letter, 18 January 1926, p. 7 ("Big poll at Keady"); Keady, Keady Urban District, 15 January 1929, printed 'N.': Witness (Belfast), 18 January 1929, p. 8 ("Keady"); also the Irish Weekly and Ulster Examiner, 19 January 1929, p. 11, and the Armagh Guardian, 18 January 1929, p. 2; Keady, Keady Urban District, 15 January 1932, printed 'Nationalists': Armagh Guardian, 8 January 1932, p. 3 ("No fight in Keady: present council unopposed")).
